Overview

About the DGX Station

NVIDIA DGX Station is a deskside AI supercomputer powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip. It brings 748 GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaFLOPS of FP4 AI compute to a single workstation, enough for models up to one trillion parameters.

It runs the same NVIDIA AI software as the data center, supports Multi-Instance GPU so several developers can share it, and includes BMC and Redfish management so IT can run it like a server.

GB300 Desktop Superchip

A Blackwell Ultra GPU and a 72-core Grace CPU joined by 900 GB/s NVLink-C2C.

748 GB coherent memory

252 GB HBM3e plus 496 GB LPDDR5X in one unified memory pool.

NVFP4 Tensor Cores

Up to 20 PFLOPS of FP4 AI compute for training and inference.

ConnectX-8 SuperNIC

Up to 800 Gb/s networking; link two DGX Stations together.

Multi-Instance GPU

Up to seven isolated instances to share the system across a team.

IT manageability

Out-of-band BMC telemetry, Redfish API and NVIDIA DCGM.
